title: Bounded Reorder Buffer for Out-of-Order Sliding Window Aggregation
description: In-memory simulation of a bounded event stream with out-of-order arrivals; compares a bounded reorder buffer against a strict forward-cursor baseline on sliding window sum accuracy.
novelty: Uses sliding windows with a bounded reorder buffer that retains late events so they contribute to all future window computations, versus a no-buffer baseline that permanently drops events once the forward time cursor passes them. Differs from the prior tumbling-window/watermark-grace project in window type, retention mechanism, and error model (cumulative drift in future windows vs single-window correction).
method: Algorithm (bounded reorder buffer): events arrive in perturbed order; an event is dropped only if event_time < max_seen_time - reorder_delay; otherwise it is inserted into an in-memory time-to-value map; the sliding window sum at each event equals the sum of stored values in [t - W, t]. Baseline (strict forward cursor): processing_time ratchets forward; any event with event_time < processing_time is permanently dropped and never contributes to any future window. Data: n_events with integer times 0..n-1, uniform values in [0,10]; arrival order is the sorted order perturbed by bounded integer displacement of at most n/8 positions (seeded). Ground truth (y): oracle window sum using ALL events in [t-W, t]. No train/test split (single-pass streaming); all events are evaluated. Metrics: window_sum_mae (lower=better, mean absolute error vs oracle), late_retention_rate (higher=better, fraction of out-of-order events not dropped), max_abs_error (lower=better). reorder_delay = n//8, W = n//8.
acceptance_tests: run_experiment(42, 256) yields metrics['window_sum_mae'] strictly less than baseline_metrics['window_sum_mae']
run_experiment(42, 256) yields metrics['late_retention_rate'] strictly greater than baseline_metrics['late_retention_rate']
make_dataset(seed=1, n_samples=31) raises ValueError because n_samples < 32
